question.text: If $\epsilon_0$ denotes the permittivity of free space and $\Phi_{\mathrm{E}}$ is the flux of the electric field through the area bounded by the closed surface, then dimension of $\left(\epsilon_0 \frac{\mathrm{~d} \phi_{\mathrm{E}}}{\mathrm{dt}}\right)$ are that of :

solution.text:
We know that formula for displacement current is given by
$\mathrm{id}=\varepsilon_0 \frac{\mathrm{~d} \phi_{\varepsilon}}{\mathrm{dt}}$
